resources.string: The three permissions below determine whether signal readings are accurate and whether background monitoring can stay alive. Here is what each one is for:
Reads signal strength and network mode, and identifies the subId of each SIM. Without it RSRP shows as unknown and the SIM card list may be empty.
Since Android 10, cellular signal strength (including SINR) counts as location-related data. Without it SINR always shows as unknown, and fake full bars detection loses one dimension.
Monitoring runs as a foreground service. Without notification permission, Android 13 and later refuses to keep a foreground service resident, and the system kills background monitoring.
The permissions below were not granted, so the related features are limited. Turn them on in system settings and they take effect as soon as you return to the app:
The system restricts background apps by default. Unless you enable the two options below, monitoring may stop working:
The system blocks auto-start by default. If you leave it off, monitoring and auto-downgrade will not resume after you restart the phone.
Otherwise the system freezes the app when the screen goes off: network quality monitoring stops, and after a switch back to 4G the original network mode may not be restored.
Open settings first opens the auto-start management page. On device models that do not have that page, it opens the app info page instead; enable both options there manually.
Request battery optimization exemption (in one step)
